rows: I know how that looked. I was there, unfortunately. I would like another go.
I can brawl, honestly. I just want to show you I can do it without falling over.
Risk? I know I have taken too many. This time I am going to plan it properly.
Time, to me, is good. I learned that the hard way, and I am not going to rush it.
The people deserve better than my last appearance. I am going to try to give them that.
I know I can do better, and I am going to show you.
I am not going to pretend the last one did not happen. I am going to move past it.
I am checking my stance, honestly. It is steadier than it was. I can tell you that much.
Technique. I am working on it. You are right to ask. Show me yours and I will show you mine.
Strikes are fine. I am learning to land them, and I am getting better.
A gamble should have a plan. Mine does now. Yours?
A stall is not for me. I would rather get stuck in.
The people want a proper contest. I am going to give them one, even if it takes me a while.
You say I am not ready. Maybe. Watch me try anyway.
You are proud of your {strength}, good for you. Good, I will try again. I will try to get round it, and I will be honest about it.
I have been working on how to handle your {strength}. It is not perfect yet, but it is better.
You are not rattling me, which helps. Good, I will try again. I am still learning how to do that.
Fair, I deserved that. I deserved that. You are right, and I will take that.
I could be embarrassed about that. I am, a little. I will still do my best.
One fall, one count. Please let it be simple. Keep me down and I will say you earned it. Fairly.
On the mat I will try to keep my feet under me. Stay close and you will see.
Grounded or standing, I am going to try my hardest.
Stand up and I will try to meet you. I want to show you the new version.
That was honest, at least. That is the kind of honesty I want to match.
Could you answer, please? I am trying. I will wait, and I will keep trying too.
Fair, I deserved that. I deserved that. I will take that as a test.
I concede that, and I am sorry for it. I will prove it at the bell.
I will give this match everything, and I will try to get it right this time.
My approach is honest and careful. You will see it on the night.
Whatever happens, I will not pretend it did not matter.
I am still going, somehow. I still have a second go to make.
I have one more try left in me, and you will see it when the bell goes.
You're right, I'm sorry. I haven't got anything specific that proves it. I'll try to do better than that.
I wanted to make a point and I got it wrong. I can't back that accusation up, so I'm taking it back.
Thanks for being straight about it. I'd much rather see what we can both do in the ring.
Fair enough. We can get past that and have a proper contest.
I'd like them to see whether I can keep my balance when things go wrong. I've been working on that.
We can find out if my preparation holds up against you. I don't need to pretend I've proved it already.
I know people have opinions about us. What can we actually show them by getting the wrestling right tonight?
I'd rather demonstrate something than make another claim. What can we give the people to judge for themselves?
You've got a way to stop my {strength}. Fair enough. I've been practising how to recover without making a complete mess of the next move.
I know my {strength} won't get me through every exchange. This time I've done some work on what happens if you manage to stop them.
That's fair. I know better than to pretend I can prove something I haven't seen.
You're right to ask for something concrete. I'd rather show you what I can do than keep repeating a claim.
I know I've got plenty left to learn. I don't think that means I have to wait for permission to beat you.
You've got the experience, fair enough. I want to show you what I've managed to learn from getting things wrong.
Experience isn't never making a mistake. It's knowing how to get out of one without making another.
I've learned to keep my head when a move goes wrong. I'd like to show you that part.
You've seen me get it wrong on tape. Fair enough. I have been working rather hard on that bit.
I hope your notes have room for an improvement or two. I'd quite like to show you some.
I study the moves I mess up, honestly. Watching the ones that work is much nicer, but less useful.
I've practised a way out of the position as well as a way in. I'd rather not get stranded in it again.
